title: DMN Decision-Core
description: Input format for the DMN generator. Sibling of the BPMN Logic-Core, deliberately shaped the same way: a flat node list plus a flat edge list. DMN 1.3 (OMG formal/21-01-01) nests requirements inside the element that requires them; the writer nests on the way out and the importer flattens on the way in, exactly as the BPMN side already does for boundary events.

$schemaVersion.description: Optional schema version (current: "1.0"). Absent or "1.0" accepted.

id.description: Definitions id. `xsd:ID` is an XML NCName, which is wider than this pattern — the same is true at every other `id` in this schema (Node, Requirement, DecisionTable, InputClause, OutputClause, DecisionRule). ASCII letters/digits/`_`/`-`/`.` are accepted, matching what a legal DMN id may need for the import path (dmn-xml-importer plan, Stage 2) to accept it; `.` was widened for exactly that reason (`my.decision` is legal DMN and was previously rejected). Full NCName also permits Unicode letters, and that is intentionally NOT accepted here: measured against dmn-moddle, a non-ASCII id like `Entscheidung_Über` writes without complaint and then fails to read back (0 drgElements, 'unparsable content', 'unresolved reference' — see CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] and scripts/dmn/import-scope.js's IM07/IM08 for the full measurement). Widening this pattern to `\p{L}` would therefore let our own pipeline emit a `.dmn` file our own importer cannot read. This is a dmn-moddle library defect, not a design choice — do not 'fix' the narrowness without re-measuring dmn-moddle first.

name.description: Definitions name. tNamedElement declares name as required, so a fallback is emitted when this is absent

namespace.description: Required by DMN13.xsd tDefinitions/@namespace. The target namespace of this decision model — an absolute URI identifying the model, not a schema location

expressionLanguage.description: Defaults to FEEL (https://www.omg.org/spec/DMN/20191111/FEEL/) when omitted. Expressions are carried as text either way — nothing here parses FEEL

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

type.description: The DRG element classes that substitute into DMN13.xsd's drgElement group. decisionService is deliberately out of scope for now — it is a grouping construct with four reference lists and its own DI divider line

name.description: Required, and not by our choice: every DRG element extends tNamedElement, which declares name use="required"

variable.description: Name of the information item this element produces. Defaults to the element name when omitted

typeRef.description: Type of the produced variable, e.g. string, number, boolean, date

usingTask.description: decision only — id(s) of the BPMN Business Rule Task(s) this decision serves. The OMG-standard direction of the BPMN<->DMN link (tDecision/usingTask, 0..unbounded); the BPMN side carries the mirror in extensionElements because BPMN 2.0 defines no attribute for it. A single string covers the common one-task case; an array covers the XSD's unbounded cardinality

usingProcess.description: decision only — id(s) of the BPMN process(es) this decision serves (tDecision/usingProcess, 0..unbounded)

decisionTable.description: decision only — decision logic as a table

expression.description: decision only — decision logic as a literal expression. Mutually exclusive with decisionTable

locationURI.description: knowledgeSource only — where the authority lives

parameters.description: businessKnowledgeModel only — the formal parameters of its encapsulated logic

body.description: businessKnowledgeModel only — the literal expression its encapsulated logic evaluates

Requirement.description: An edge of the decision requirement graph. source/target read in FLOW direction: the required element is the source, the requiring element is the target. The XML nests the requirement under the target.

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

type.description: information: decision|inputData -> decision. knowledge: businessKnowledgeModel -> decision|businessKnowledgeModel. authority: decision|inputData|knowledgeSource -> knowledgeSource|decision

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

hitPolicy.description: Defaults to UNIQUE. Note bpmn-io's dmn-moddle drops hitPolicy="UNIQUE" on write because it is the schema default, while keeping preferredOrientation="Rule-as-Row" which is also a default — relevant to golden files, not to meaning

outputs.description: At least one is mandatory: DMN13.xsd gives tDecisionTable/output no minOccurs, so it defaults to 1

annotations.description: Rule annotation COLUMNS (headers). Note tRuleAnnotationClause carries only a name — unlike almost everything else in DMN it does not extend tDMNElement and therefore has no id

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

expression.description: The value being tested, as text. Not parsed

allowedValues.description: Unary tests constraining the input domain, as text

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

name.description: Required when the table has more than one output clause

id.description: xsd:ID (NCName), narrowed to ASCII — see the root `id` field's description for why.

documentation.description: Serialised as tDMNElement/description. A rule is the one part of a decision table Decision-Core lets you document, and that is a deliberate line rather than an oversight: a rule's rationale ("why does this row exist") is business content a reader of a foreign file is looking for, while a DecisionTable's own description restates the decision that owns it — so `DecisionTable.description` stays an IM05 loss (see scripts/dmn/import-scope.js) and this one is carried.

when.description: One unary test per input clause, in order. Text, not parsed

then.description: One result expression per output clause, in order

annotations.description: One entry per annotation column, in order
